text: dsh-code-git-workbench 是 DeepSeek Harness Web UI 的代码与 Git 工作台，在右侧栏注册 Code 和 Git 页面，并由宿主端提供同源工作区与 Git 接口。Code 页面提供目录树、文件标签和代码编辑，可查看、修改并保存工作区文件；Git 页面显示分支、提交图、提交详情和文件差异，并支持检出、合并、变基、提交挑选、重置、撤销、标签及远端同步。插件还会将正在运行的子 agent 排在目录列表前。适合在 DSH 网页界面编辑项目文件、查看版本历史和管理分支的用户。代码没有声明 API Key 或外部服务账号要求。

dsh-code-git-workbench adds Code and Git pages to the DSH Web UI sidebar. Code browses and edits workspace files. Git displays branches, commits, and diffs, and supports checkout, merge, rebase, reset, tags, and remote sync. It also sorts running subagents first. No API key is declared.
想直接在 DSH 里浏览工作区文件并编辑保存。
有没有能在侧边栏查看分支和提交记录的工作台？
I want to inspect commit history and compare file changes from my DSH workspace.
dsh-code-git-workbench 的功能「工作区代码编辑」：在右侧 Code 页面浏览目录、打开文件标签并使用代码编辑器修改内容；保存按钮和自动保存会通过工作区文件接口写回文件。
dsh-code-git-workbench 的功能「Git 图形工作台」：在右侧 Git 页面查看分支、提交图、提交详情和文件差异，并从界面执行分支检出、合并、变基、重置等版本操作。
dsh-code-git-workbench 使用 Git fetch、pull 和 push 与当前仓库配置的远端交互；这些同步操作会连接对应远端，代码未指定固定服务地址。（见 index.mjs:884-930）

dsh-code-git-workbench README · dsh-code-git-workbench：A Code and Git workbench for the **DeepSeek Harness Web UI**. It adds two pages
to the right Sidebar:

- **Code** — a lazy file tree for a Harness workspace, file tabs, a CodeMirror
  editor, syntax highlighting, search, reload and save.
- **Git** — a PyCharm-style log: local/remote branches, a commit graph, commit
  details, file diffs, checkout, merge, rebase, cherry-pick, reset, revert, tags
  and fetch/pull/push.

dsh-code-git-workbench README · dsh-code-git-workbench：It also keeps running subagents above idle ones in the header's subagent catalog
popup.

The plugin is host + client code for DeepSeek Harness. It has no build step and
no dependency on VS Code. The PyCharm-style Git UI is shared in source form with
the companion VS Code extension
[pycharm-git-log](https://github.com/DazzzleKK/pycharm-git-log); the two
repositories remain independent at runtime.

dsh-code-git-workbench README · Requirements：- DeepSeek Harness with the bundled plugin CLI (tested on the 0.2.1-rc.2 /
  DSH 44.x desktop build).
- A local Git repository for the Git page.
- Node.js is **not** required to install or run the plugin.

dsh-code-git-workbench README · Install：Clone this repository somewhere permanent, then register the folder as a local
plugin in the `desktop` profile.

dsh-code-git-workbench README · Windows：```powershell
$repo = "C:\path\to\dsh-code-git-workbench"
$cli = "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\DeepSeek Harness\resources\runtime\cli\bin\dsh.cmd"
& $cli plugin --profile desktop add "link:$repo"
```

dsh-code-git-workbench README · macOS / Linux：Use the `dsh` CLI that ships with the application. Its exact path depends on the
install layout; with the CLI already on `PATH`:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add link:/absolute/path/to/dsh-code-git-workbench
```

Fully quit and reopen DeepSeek Harness. A window reload is not enough: the host
half is loaded at process start.

To use it in the browser profile instead:

```bash
dsh --profile web
```

and install with `--profile web`.

dsh-code-git-workbench README · Update：```bash
git pull
```

Then restart DeepSeek Harness. There is nothing to compile.

dsh-code-git-workbench README · Uninstall：```powershell
& $cli plugin --profile desktop remove dsh-code-git-workbench
```

Restart the application afterwards.

dsh-code-git-workbench README · Use：1. Open a session. The pages start from the session's workspace; Code can switch
   to any Harness workspace, Git to any workspace that is a Git repository.
2. Open the right Sidebar (`Ctrl+Alt+B` on the desktop build, or the sidebar
   button).
3. Click `+` → **Code** or **Git**. The guide also lists both pages.
4. For more room, use the panel's fullscreen control.

dsh-code-git-workbench README · Code：- Lazy directory tree; `.git` is hidden.
- The workspace selector in the tree header lists every Harness workspace. When
  the session directory is not a repository, Code starts in the first workspace
  that is one. The choice is remembered per session.
- Tabs keep their own document, cursor, scroll position and dirty state.
- **Autosave** is on, modelled after PyCharm:
  - idle for 2 seconds after the last edit — every dirty tab is written;
  - switching to another application / hiding the DSH window;
  - closing a file tab (the tab is saved, not discarded);
  - switching the workspace (all dirty tabs are saved first);
  - quitting the page (`pagehide`, keepalive request);
  - clicking another DSH tab (for example Git) blurs the editor and triggers a
    save, which covers the “before VCS operation” case.
  Switching between file tabs does **not** force a save; the idle/focus/close
  triggers do, just like PyCharm. `Ctrl+S` still saves manually; the status bar
  shows `Auto-saved` after a successful write.
- `Ctrl+R` reloads the active file. The toolbar has Save and Reload actions.
- CodeMirror offers line numbers, bracket matching, auto-close,

dsh-code-git-workbench README · Git：- Repository selector for every workspace that is a Git repository.
- Branch tree with local/remote groups, filter, current branch, ahead/behind,
  checkout, checkout + rebase, merge, rebase, compare, push, rename, delete and
  tag actions.
- Slash-separated branch names become expandable folders: `feat/123-login` is
  shown as `feat` → `123-login`. The tree is built independently inside Local
  and Remote. With a single remote, its name is treated as context and stripped
  from the folder path; with several remotes, the remote name becomes the first
  folder. Folder expansion is remembered per repository.
- Branches can be starred from the row or from the context menu. Favorites float
  to the top of their own folder (and of the Local/Remote root); the choice is
  stored per Git repository in the browser profile and survives tab/page reloads.
- Commit log for the selected branch (or all branches) with the colored graph,
  ref badges, author and date; filter and “load more”.
- Commit details with the full message, parents, files and `+/-`, plus checkout,
  branch, cherry-pick, merge, rebase, reset (soft/mixed/hard), revert and tag.
- File rows op

dsh-code-git-workbench README · Subagent order：The header's descendant-count button opens the subagent catalog. Running rows
are moved above idle rows after every render, per tree level. The sort is a DOM
enhancement because the shipped catalog has no slot for ordering; host state is
not modified.

dsh-code-git-workbench README · Architecture：```
index.mjs         host half: /code-git static UI + JSON API
client.js         client half: Sidebar tab types + subagent catalog sort
web/code/         vanilla JS + CodeMirror 5 (vendored)
web/git/          PyCharm-style Git UI

The host API applies `ctx.connection.requestRejection(req)` to every request, so
it inherits the Harness Host/Origin fence and browser authentication. All routes
are same-origin:

dsh-code-git-workbench README · Architecture：- the desktop shell forwards `dsh-app://app/code-git/...` to the local host with
  the host cookie;
- a browser talks to the same listener directly.

API surface:

dsh-code-git-workbench README · Architecture：| Route | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /code-git/api/context` | session cwd, selected root, workspaces, repo status |
| `GET /code-git/api/tree` | one directory level |
| `GET/PUT /code-git/api/file` | read/write one file |
| `GET /code-git/api/git/state` | branches, commits, refs, ahead/behind |
| `GET /code-git/api/git/status` | staged, unstaged and untracked files |
| `GET /code-git/api/git/worktree-diff` | index/HEAD/working tree file contents |
| `GET /code-git/api/git/commit` | commit message, parents, file stats |
| `GET /code-git/api/git/diff` | old/new file contents |
| `POST /code-git/api/git/action` | checkout, merge, rebase, reset, fetch, pull branch, push, … |

dsh-code-git-workbench README · Architecture：Every request is checked against the session's registered workspaces; paths are
resolved and confined to the selected root. Git runs through `execFile` without
a shell, with `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`.

The Git UI is the same HTML/CSS/JS as the companion VS Code extension's panel.
`web/git/bridge.js` implements the small `acquireVsCodeApi()` surface the UI was
written against and maps its messages to the JSON API. No VS Code runtime is
involved.

dsh-code-git-workbench README · Development：There is no build step:

- host: edit `index.mjs`, restart the host;
- client: edit `client.js`, restart the host (or use a web profile with live
  patch reload);
- Code UI: edit `web/code/`;
- Git UI: edit `web/git/`.

For a disposable test instance:

```powershell
$cli = "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\DeepSeek Harness\resources\runtime\cli\bin\dsh.cmd"
& $cli --profile web --port 3080 --no-open
```

Open the printed token URL and use the normal UI.

Test checklist before a release:

dsh-code-git-workbench README · Limits：- No LSP, quick-open or file watchers; use the toolbar refresh.
- Custom keyboard shortcuts are not used: the DSH Web shortcut adapter accepts
  only its built-in catalog (`Unsupported Web shortcut` otherwise), so the pages
  are opened from the `+` guide.
- Edits are saved as-is; no format-on-save and no external-change merge.
- Only workspaces registered in Harness can be selected; arbitrary directories
  are rejected by the host.
- Reset/delete/push happen after their confirmation prompts; there is no undo
  inside the panel.
- Subagent sorting is a DOM enhancement, not a host catalog change.
